summary: Extends RFC 1006, which runs ISO transport over TCP, to cover ISO Transport Class 2 without the use of explicit flow control. It supplements the existing definitions rather than repeating them. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A small extra rule for running an old kind of network conversation over the Internet's ordinary delivery service.

subtitle: How to run ISO Transport Class 2, without explicit flow control, over TCP port 399.

tldr.problem: RFC 1006 carries only ISO Transport Class 0 over TCP, but some users need separate normal and expedited data channels and an explicit disconnect.
tldr.mechanism: This memo adds ISO 8073 Transport Class 2, non-use of explicit flow control, on top of TCP. It reuses the RFC 1006 packet header, listens on TCP port 399, and may use a second TCP connection for expedited data.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational supplement to RFC 1006 and also describes DECnet over TCP/IP. It repeats no protocol text from RFC 1006 or ISO 8073 and must be read alongside them.

today: RFC 1859 is an Informational memo from October 1995, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It supplements RFC 1006, which it must be read with.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 1859 is an extension to RFC 1006 (STD 35). It does not duplicate the protocol definitions in RFC 1006 or in ISO 8073, and it should be used together with them.

RFC 1006 defines how to implement ISO 8073 Transport Class 0 on top of TCP. This memo defines Class 2, non-use of explicit flow control. Like Class 0, it provides a basic connection with minimal overhead. It suits cases where separate virtual data channels for normal and expedited data are wanted, or where an explicit disconnection is wanted.

Hosts that implement the extension are expected to listen on well-known TCP port 399. Port 102, the RFC 1006 port, is recommended not to be used, to minimise impact on existing RFC 1006 implementations.
sections.eli5: An old messaging system already had one way to ride on the Internet. This note adds a second way, with its own front door, so the first way keeps working undisturbed.

sections.title: TCP as the Network Service
sections.content:
The protocol is fundamentally ISO 8073 Class 2 with no explicit flow control, plus three points: expedited data is supported, splitting and recombining may be used for expedited data, and the network service is provided by TCP. The RFC recommends not using the multiplexing that Class 2 allows, for performance reasons.

ISO transport exchanges TPDUs (transport protocol data units). Here they are wrapped in TPKTs. The mapping from network service primitives to TCP is straightforward and repeated from RFC 1006: an N-DATA.REQUEST becomes a TCP send, and an N-DATA.INDICATION is a data-ready event followed by a read. Only the called and calling addresses (the server's and client's 4-octet IP addresses) are mapped; other parameters are ignored.
sections.eli5: The old system speaks in little envelopes. Here each envelope is dropped into a pipe that carries a stream of bytes, and the receiver reads the envelopes back out in order.

sections.title: Connecting and Disconnecting
sections.content:
To connect, the initiator makes an active TCP open to the desired IP address on port 399, and a server listens on that port. The Connection Request and Connection Confirmation TPDUs may negotiate the use of expedited data, but must not negotiate explicit flow control.

Release follows ISO 8073, and there are two kinds. A Synchronous Disconnect requires all messages at the source to be sent and all at the destination to be delivered first; its reason code is normal (80 hex). An Abort Disconnect has no such requirement; it uses the normal reason with an additional information value of c0 hex. Disconnect Request and Disconnect Confirmation TPDUs are exchanged in both cases, and receipt of the confirmation closes the TCP connection.
sections.eli5: Hanging up can be polite, where both sides finish their sentences first, or abrupt, where one side just drops the call. The note names a code for each way.

sections.title: Expedited Data and Splitting
sections.content:
Expedited data may be used if it was negotiated at connection time. In this mode it needs no Expedited Data Acknowledgement. Splitting and recombining lets one transport connection use several TCP connections, so expedited data travels on its own.

The RFC recommends creating the second TCP connection only when expedited data is actually requested. Expedited data must be sent only over an outgoing TCP connection, and that connection must not be shared among transport connections. It stays up until the transport connection ends, and is then closed.

The implementors' note explains why: a congested normal-data TCP connection then cannot block the expedited one, and the two are independent.
sections.eli5: Urgent messages get their own private lane, so a traffic jam in the normal lane cannot hold them up.

sections.title: The TPKT Header
sections.content:
TCP carries a continuous stream of octets with no boundaries, while ISO transport expects discrete units. As in RFC 1006, each packet (TPKT) has a packet header followed by a TPDU. This memo keeps that scheme and does not change the version number, since the TPDU itself shows which transport class is in use.

The header has a vrsn field of 8 bits, always 3; a reserved octet; and a 16-bit packet length that counts the whole packet including the header, with a minimum of 7 and a maximum of 65535. The TPDU format is defined in ISO 8073.
sections.eli5: Because the pipe is just one long stream of bytes, each envelope gets a small label saying how long it is, so the reader knows where one ends and the next begins.

sections.title: DECnet over TCP/IP
sections.content:
DECnet over TCP/IP is implemented by running the DECnet Session Control layer over this extension. The extension provides the Transport Service features that DECnet applications need.

Session Control offers end users separate virtual channels called Normal and Expedited, and needs the transport layer to keep them independent: expedited transmission must not be blocked by a congested normal channel. It also requires that all data in transit be delivered before the transport connection is released, which matches the Synchronous Disconnect. Security issues are not discussed in this memo.
sections.eli5: One computer maker's network needed two independent lanes and a tidy goodbye. This note shows how to get both over the Internet.
